title: City Lights
synopsis: A tramp, a blind flower girl, a drunken millionaire who only remembers you at night, and a small coin that decides everything.

nodes.text: A bronze hand on which you have been sleeping.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Salute” back. Polite shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Smart.

nodes.text: A girl, blind, who mistakes you for a fine gentleman.

choices.consequence: “Buy a flower” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Heart.
There is no taking “Walk past” back. Cold shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: A man with a rope and a brick around his neck.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Stop him.” The story records the instinct as “Brave” and carries it forward.
“Hand him a flower” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Polite.

nodes.text: He insists you stay, drives like a maniac, calls you brother.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Stay the night” back. Brave shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Wise.

nodes.text: Sober, he does not know you and a butler shows you the door.

nodes.text: The smallest possible smile, and the last shot of a movie that does not need to say more.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Smile back” back. Heart shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
There is no taking “Look down” back. Honest shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
Some endings reveal themselves last.

nodes.text: She closes her fingers around yours and laughs and laughs, and you both stand in the doorway of a flower shop that smells of gardenia and the future.
You go before she can be ashamed and the bell on her door rings behind you and the street takes you back. The film ends on a frame of empty pavement.
You become her quiet best customer, never said for what you are. She finds out, decades later, from a letter in a drawer.
